proposed_edges.relationship: ‘Fear and Anxiety: Writing about Emotion in Modern History’ (2003) appraises emotionology, social constructivism, narrativization and psycho-historical methods and, using fear as its example, argues that insufficient attention has been paid to physiology and to how emotions mediate between the individual and the social; it characterizes a new history of the emotions as ‘aesthesiology’ (article abstract).
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Abstract only, read on the publisher page (History Workshop Journal 55, 2003, 111–133, doi 10.1093/hwj/55.1.111) and in the Birkbeck eprint record (no full text deposited). The abstract says the article ‘examines and appraises some approaches to the analysis of emotional experience in history’ (emotionology, social constructivism, narrativization, psychohistory), finds that ‘insufficient attention has been paid to physiology’ and to emotions' mediating role, argues via fear and anxiety that emotions are ‘fundamentally concerned with power relations’, and defines ‘aesthesiology’ as ‘the emotional reaction of the self to stimuli in lived experience’. The body is unread (paywall), so the claim is bounded to the abstract: which authors she criticizes, and how, is not established. A critique within the field she contributes to; edge_2841 (contribution) remains.

review.reason: Abstract re-read verbatim in the Birkbeck eprint record (full text not deposited; OUP DOI is the citation URL; acceptable). Supports 'examines and appraises' four approaches and 'insufficient attention has been paid to physiology and how emotions mediate between the individual and the social' and the definition of aesthesiology. Claim is properly bounded to the abstract in the evidence note. One overreach in the relationship: 'proposing aesthesiology instead' implies a replacement of the appraised approaches; the abstract says only 'A new history of the emotions can be characterized as aesthesiology'. Edit the relationship to the abstract's wording and flag it as abstract-based. Distinct from edge_2841 (contribution).
